edition.en: The complete oration, from the second edition (Boston: James Munroe and Company, 1838), as transcribed from a scan on English Wikisource; the title page is omitted and paragraphs split across pages are rejoined. A leftover line-break hyphen (“in-corruption”) is closed up and one misprint of the 1838 printing (“Marveil” for Marvell) is corrected.
edition.zh: 演讲全文，据英文维基文库依扫描本所录的第二版（波士顿：詹姆斯·芒罗公司，1838）；略去扉页，被分页切断的段落已重新接合。合上一处残留的换行连字符（in-corruption），并改正 1838 年印本的一处排印错误（Marvell 误作 Marveil）。

basis.en: Delivered in 1837 and printed in 1837 and 1838; Ralph Waldo Emerson died in 1882.
basis.zh: 1837 年演讲，1837 年与 1838 年印行；爱默生卒于 1882 年。

note.en: Emerson’s address to the Phi Beta Kappa Society at Harvard in 1837, on what a scholar is for: not a bookworm but “Man Thinking”. Its second part is the best short account here of how to use a library without being used by it: books are “the best of things, well used; abused, among the worst”, and their one purpose is to inspire. Notice the lamps: when our own light fails, we go to the lamps that were kindled by older light. The Chinese translates the whole address.
note.zh: 爱默生 1837 年在哈佛对斐陶斐荣誉学会的演讲，讲学者为了什么：不是书虫，而是“思考着的人”。它的第二部分，是本架关于怎样使用图书馆、而不被图书馆所用的最好的短论：书“用得好，是最好的东西；用得不好，是最坏的东西之一”，它的唯一用处是激发。请留意那些灯：当我们自己的光熄灭时，就去寻那些由更早的光点燃的灯。中文译出演讲全文。

excerpt.orig: Books are the best of things, well used; abused, among the worst.
excerpt.en: Books are the best of things, well used; abused, among the worst.
excerpt.zh: 书用得好，是最好的东西；用得不好，是最坏的东西之一。

gloss.en: Emerson gave this address to the Phi Beta Kappa Society at Cambridge, Massachusetts, on 31 August 1837.
gloss.zh: 爱默生于 1837 年 8 月 31 日在马萨诸塞州剑桥，对斐陶斐荣誉学会发表这篇演讲。

gloss.at: the star in the constellation Harp
gloss.en: Vega, in Lyra. Because Earth’s axis slowly precesses, Vega will lie near the north celestial pole in roughly twelve thousand years.
gloss.zh: 天琴座的织女星。由于地轴缓慢的岁差运动，大约一万两千年后，织女星将靠近北天极。

gloss.en: John Flamsteed (1646–1719), the first Astronomer Royal, and William Herschel (1738–1822), who discovered Uranus; both made great catalogues of the stars.
gloss.zh: 约翰·弗兰斯蒂德（1646–1719），英国第一任皇家天文学家；威廉·赫歇尔（1738–1822），天王星的发现者。两人都编过重要的星表。

gloss.at: Wherever Macdonald sits, there is the head of the table
gloss.en: A Highland saying about the chief of Clan Macdonald: the place of honour is wherever he sits. Versions of it are told of other chiefs.
gloss.zh: 苏格兰高地关于麦克唐纳氏族族长的一句俗语：他坐在哪里，哪里就是上座。类似的说法也被安在别的族长身上。

gloss.at: Sicklied o'er with the pale cast of thought
gloss.en: From Hamlet’s soliloquy “To be, or not to be” (Act III, scene 1).
gloss.zh: 出自《哈姆雷特》第三幕第一场“生存还是毁灭”的独白。

gloss.en: Johann Heinrich Pestalozzi (1746–1827), the Swiss educational reformer.
gloss.zh: 约翰·亨利希·裴斯泰洛齐（1746–1827），瑞士教育改革家。

note.en: Emerson’s call for ‘Man Thinking’ helped set the terms of American intellectual life; the part on books is wise, the rest more stirring than precise.
note.zh: 爱默生呼唤“思考着的人”，为美国的思想生活定下基调；论书一节睿智，其余激励多于精确。
